editorial.headline: Agro-Tourism Is Open Nationally, but Closed to PMA Registration in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This activity turns farms, fisheries and livestock settings into visitor experiences—nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet blocked for PMA registration across Bali.
editorial.body:
Agro-tourism turns agricultural landscapes and practices into the reason to visit. It covers the management of tourism attractions built around food-crop and horticultural cultivation, plantations, fisheries and livestock, where the agricultural setting is the principal visitor draw. The experience may be recreational, educational or participatory: guests might encounter cultivation, agricultural learning, conservation, product processing or the cultural value of local farming communities as part of a tourism offering.

The scope is broad enough to accommodate a carefully composed destination rather than a single activity. It includes production, collection, conservation, cultivation, processing and agricultural education when they support the tourism function. Supporting facilities may include food and beverage services, visitor-interaction areas and places to sell agricultural products. Fruit gardens, plantation visits, coffeenery concepts and winery concepts all sit comfortably within that tourism-led frame. What matters is the developed visitor function: agriculture conducted solely to produce commodities, without that tourism dimension, is outside this activity.

Nationally, the position is direct. The activity is **TERBUKA** for PMA and carries a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling. It is open across Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar scales, so the national classification does not itself limit participation to a particular business size. For a founder assessing the activity at national level, the record supports a fully foreign-owned PMA structure.

Bali changes the practical answer completely. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. At the Besar scale, every scope is classified in OSS as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah risk, placing it within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI. The Bali status is **BLOCCATO_CLASSE_RISCHIO**: this is not a reduction in the national ownership ceiling, but a block on PMA registration in the province. The national openness therefore remains real, while Bali’s current rule prevents a PMA from using this activity there.
editorial.pullQuote: National openness remains real, but Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium prevents PMA registration for this activity on the island.
